Budget against successful tasks using your actual cache discounts and retry costs, then compare providers on that basis.

Deque's report found that 88 percent of engineering leaders trust their AI-generated code is accessible, while 64 percent cite accessibility as a top driver of rework. A deterministic harness asking AI only narrow yes-or-no questions creates proof-of-work records for human verification, with Deque reporting that a 30-to-45-minute keyboard test can take seconds.

articles.headline: The State of Typography in Design Systems
articles.blurb: A survey of 94 UX and product designers found that 78% can easily change or suggest fonts, while brand alignment is the leading consideration when choosing typefaces, followed by accessibility. Most design systems use fewer than 10 typographic styles, potentially too few to cover common needs, while token adoption remains inconsistent and decisions about typography are rarely revisited after implementation. Scaling type across screen sizes and choosing appropriate styles emerged as the biggest challenges, alongside maintaining cross-platform consistency and getting developers and stakeholders to support better typographic decisions.

articles.headline: For a brief generation or two, we clicked
articles.blurb: Graphical interfaces made clicking and tapping a temporary language humans had to learn to communicate with computers, while conversational AI may return interaction to the far older and more natural behavior of simply saying what we want.

articles.headline: The Senior Art Director Behind Assassin's Creed's Visual Identity Shares His Personal Sketches
articles.blurb: Montreal art director Raphaël Lacoste, who shaped Assassin's Creed's visual identity at Ubisoft, shares personal sketches and monumental landscape paintings that echo 19th-century Romantic painters like Caspar David Friedrich.

articles.headline: How Gen Z Is Changing Packaging
articles.blurb: Brands are moving from safe, minimal packaging toward designs Gen Z wants to display and collect, since the package stays visible in content long after purchase. Mane wraps heat protectants and smoothing products in consistent pink packaging that makes the whole line recognizable before anyone reads a label. Touchland keeps its sanitizer format fixed while rotating limited character collaborations, and Reale Actives pairs playful names like Go Calm with clear descriptions of what each product does.

articles.headline: YouTube Culture & Trends Report: How Technology Is Changing Personal Expression
articles.blurb: AI is becoming a tool for personal expression rather than just content production. 72% of video posters aged 14-44 have used AI to create or edit images or videos, and 61% are interested in using AI to insert themselves into content. Creators use AI to restore childhood memories, and hobbyists turn fashion sketches into realistic designs and bring fan fiction to life.

articles.headline: Win Report: How a simpler homepage increased sales by 24%
articles.blurb: The Raw Honey Shop increased sales by 24% by simplifying its homepage and making key selling points easier to find. The original page buried product information and trust signals in lengthy brand storytelling, and 50% of desktop visitors never reached the products section. The redesign replaced long paragraphs with a scannable checklist of product benefits, connected a beekeeper's photo to a specific trust claim, and added a “Shop our honeys” button near the top of the page. The test shows how clear value propositions and prominent calls to action can help visitors make purchase decisions with less effort.

articles.headline: How to Create Links for SEO Google Can't Ignore
articles.blurb: Build links from topically relevant sites rather than chasing volume. Place links high in article text with descriptive surrounding context and natural anchors that reflect each page's unique purpose. Earn independent editorial links that add new information instead of relying on sitewide links or mass syndication. Space link-building efforts over time and keep the source page, anchor text, surrounding content, and destination closely aligned. Avoid redirects or content changes that weaken a page's topical relevance.

articles.headline: Should you hard-code your website and run it from GitHub? (Webinar)
articles.blurb: Vector's VP of Marketing Jess Cook and ércule founder Justin Dunham share what they learned from moving a live website to GitHub. They'll explain why Vector left its CMS and how the team managed the migration alongside a rebrand. The webinar covers launch challenges and lessons from the first 30 days.

articles.headline: We Tested Microsoft Clarity to Understand Bot Traffic and Citations
articles.blurb: Microsoft Clarity adds useful AI visibility data to your marketing measurement stack by tracking bot activity, AI citations, and website usability issues. Brainlabs found that AI bots generated 27,190 requests between September 1 and September 28, representing 13.15% of measured traffic, but crawling activity did not necessarily translate into referral visits. Its Topic Insights feature also found gaps in citations for nonbranded prompts related to AI search measurement and agentic enablement. Session recordings can connect technical errors and user behavior to specific problems, such as a failing form that prevented clients from submitting feedback. The tool is free, but its AI visibility features are in beta and require carefully chosen prompts, relevant integrations, and validation against other analytics data.

articles.headline: How to summarize your next meeting with Granola
articles.blurb: Granola lets users save prompts as recipes and run them by typing/followed by the recipe name. This post provides a prompt that distills meeting notes into two bullets under 12 words each, focusing on the 80% that matters most and the remaining 20% of key decisions or actions. Create separate recipes for different meeting types since sales calls and 1:1s need different summaries.

articles.headline: Is email marketing dead? No, but everything has changed
articles.blurb: Email marketing still builds valuable audience relationships, even as open and click rates become less reliable measures of performance. Apple's Mail Privacy Protection inflates opens, while AI summaries can answer subscribers' questions without a click, making email's influence harder to track. Treat your email list as an audience to nurture rather than a pipeline of customers to convert, especially since roughly 95% of the B2B market is out of market at any given time. Measure performance across quarters using branded search, retention, replies, referrals, leads, and sales instead of relying on opens and clicks.

articles.headline: The Form Before the Answer: How ChatGPT Questions Buyers Before Recommending Anything
articles.blurb: 79.4% of buying prompts trigger a follow-up questionnaire before recommendations. Most forms arrive pre-filled, with 89.7% of budget questions defaulting to the middle price range. Brands can use these forms to identify the criteria ChatGPT uses to narrow choices. Track them across repeated prompts and markets, then align product content with those criteria and ensure current prices and purchase links are easy for AI to retrieve.

articles.headline: 3 New Studies Suggest AI Visibility & Search Not Worth Investing In
articles.blurb: ChatGPT drove just 0.62% of Google organic's traffic across 145 million sessions, organic beat all AI assistants 39x in a second study, and a third found no AI lift in branded search.

articles.headline: How Harvey is Building a Frontier Marketing Org
articles.blurb: Harvey's marketing team used agents to make a tailored product film for each of hundreds of target accounts.

articles.headline: Content marketing as we knew it is over
articles.blurb: Old content marketing relied on SEO and gated content, while the new playbook prioritizes creators, founder perspectives, and short-form content.

articles.headline: Checkout.com expands into in-person payments
articles.blurb: After 14 years focused purely on online payments, Checkout.com is moving into in-store payments, citing demand from enterprise merchants who want its online acquiring performance in physical stores. The offering is software-led and device-agnostic, so merchants can keep their existing terminals, and online plus in-person run through one acquiring relationship with the same Unified Payments API, contract, and settlement. Mollie (350K+ merchants) is the launch partner, keeping control of its hardware and customer experience while running on Checkout.com's acquiring rails.

articles.headline: JPMorgan announces $5 billion in investments in companies critical to US national security
articles.blurb: JPMorgan said it had invested $5 billion of its own equity in venture, growth, and later-stage companies spanning advanced manufacturing, energy, supply chains, and defense technology. The deployment, alongside roughly $230 billion already financed through its broader initiative, shows large banks competing to fund AI infrastructure, automation, and other industries tied to US industrial policy

articles.headline: Ramp applies for national trust bank charter from OCC
articles.blurb: Ramp applied to the OCC for a national trust bank charter that would let it offer fiduciary investment management and digital-asset custody under a federal framework, while not taking deposits or making commercial loans. The application comes just after Ramp raised $1.85 billion at a $60 billion valuation and amid growing legal and industry debate over the OCC's recent wave of trust-charter approvals for fintech and crypto companies.

articles.headline: Nubank makes its mark in the US and more (26 minute podcast)
articles.blurb: In this podcast episode, Brett King sits down with Carl Rivera, Chief Product Officer at Nubank—one of the world's largest digital banking platforms—to discuss how Nubank is redefining modern banking. With customer-centricity at its core, Nu continues to pave new paths in financial services. King and Rivera discuss Nubank's exponential growth, international expansion, US market entry, design philosophy, and product strategy. They also explore Nubank's recent launch and leap forward with Nu Global, a multi-currency digital account for people with global lives.

articles.headline: Fintech funding fell 21% in Q3 as deals grew scarcer
articles.blurb: Global fintech funding fell 21% year over year to $10.6 billion in Q3 2026, while deal count dropped 31% to its lowest level since at least 2018, showing that capital is concentrating in fewer companies and larger rounds. Investors are increasingly separating AI-driven market leaders from the rest, favoring infrastructure, payments, stablecoin rails, and agentic commerce, while demanding stronger growth, efficiency, and proof of durable demand from companies without clear momentum.

articles.headline: Finance is entering its mod era
articles.blurb: Personal AI agents will become a primary channel for banking, the way mobile did, as customers want their own agent to use a bank's product rather than open its app. Letting others build on your product can be good business, since trust, data, and integrations stay with the provider. There is an emerging protocol stack for authenticating agents and restricting what they can do. Reg E liability for agent actions remains a grey area. Start with customers already asking for agent access and give them limited, revocable, enforceable permissions.

articles.headline: Visa, BILL, and Billtrust launch live pilot for trusted AI agent payments
articles.blurb: Visa, BILL, and Billtrust launched a live pilot that lets authorized AI agents complete already-approved B2B invoice payments end-to-end across supplier portals, removing a manual payment step that often still requires human login and data entry. Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol authenticates the agent and uses tokenized payment credentials, while buyer-defined controls and supplier acceptance rules remain in place, showing how agentic payments can automate AP execution without giving agents independent payment authority.

articles.headline: Anthropic's new AI agent purchases business supplies
articles.blurb: Claude Duet checks connected apps for updates and keeps working while users are offline, asking for approval before sending messages, making payments, or deleting anything. Available by waitlist to US Pro and Max subscribers, it supports checkout through Shopify's Shop Pay and Stripe's Link, with Link requiring spending approval and using virtual cards to keep real card numbers private.

articles.headline: Mastercard opens early access to AI agent payments following pilots with Coinbase, Base, and Cloudflare
articles.blurb: Mastercard opened early access to Agent Pay for Machines, giving developers APIs, a toolkit, and a sandbox for machine-to-machine payments after pilots with firms including Coinbase, Base, Cloudflare, BVNK, and Ant International. In one demo, an AI agent completed nine purchases using Coinbase's x402 protocol, Coinbase wallet infrastructure, and Base settlement, while Mastercard and BVNK handled payment orchestration across fiat and stablecoins, showing how agents could autonomously buy digital services within preset spending controls.

articles.headline: PayPal CEO says company needs faster decisions and clearer accountability
articles.blurb: PayPal CEO Enrique Lores says the company became too slow and layered under prior leadership, and his turnaround plan centers on reducing management layers, clarifying accountability, and investing more heavily in Venmo, Braintree, and consumer financial services. PayPal is also modernizing its technology stack with AI and preparing for agentic commerce, although Lores expects meaningful agent-driven transaction volume to remain limited until around 2028.

articles.headline: Ramp bolsters treasury management capabilities with Vesto acquisition
articles.blurb: Vesto gives businesses a consolidated view of accounts held across more than 12,000 institutions, adding cash-flow monitoring and forecasting to Ramp's checking and investment products. Coming immediately after Ramp's national trust-bank application and $1.85 billion financing, the acquisition advances its shift from expense management toward a broader financial operating system.

articles.headline: 23% of US consumers comfortable with agentic purchases
articles.blurb: A Money20/20 panel featuring Visa, Stripe, and Cross River explored fraud prevention, shopper control, and accountability as AI assistants move from recommending products to handling payments.

articles.headline: Britain seeks to break Apple's grip on contactless payments
articles.blurb: Britain's competition regulator proposed substantially lower access fees and fewer technical restrictions for companies using the iPhone's contactless technology.

articles.headline: Passkeys and Agentic Checkout: Vladyslav Kolodistyi on Authenticating Payments
articles.blurb: When an agent handles checkout, authentication moves from the payment itself to the mandate the customer grants the agent.

articles.headline: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud
articles.blurb: OpenAI and Google Cloud are partnering to bring OpenAI frontier models and Codex agentic workflows into Google Cloud's Model Garden. Customers will be able to purchase the models through the Google Cloud Marketplace and draw down GCP commitments, with general availability planned in the coming weeks. Microsoft remains OpenAI's primary cloud partner.

articles.headline: Google Cloud and NVIDIA Announce General Availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Infrastructure
articles.blurb: Google Cloud and NVIDIA announced the general availability of infrastructure powered by the NVIDIA Vera Rubin architecture, featuring A5X instances designed for large-scale reinforcement learning and agentic inference. Additionally, Google Cloud plans to offer NVIDIA Confidential Computing at rack scale on bare metal instances and expand confidential capabilities across virtual machine offerings.

articles.headline: DeepSeek reportedly raises $15 billion to challenge US AI labs
articles.blurb: DeepSeek reportedly raised approximately $15 billion in one of China's largest funding rounds, with Tencent and battery manufacturer CATL among the backers. The funding strengthens its push to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic as the company prepares for a potential IPO and faces growing US restrictions over security concerns.

articles.headline: Why AI infrastructure spending forecasts disagree so dramatically
articles.blurb: This comparison examines forecasts from 12 research and financial firms, explaining how different definitions produce vastly different estimates of AI infrastructure spending. It connects those projections to hyperscaler budgets, power availability, and the revenue needed to justify the buildout.

articles.headline: How GitHub is rebuilding Git infrastructure for AI agents
articles.blurb: GitHub has placed copies of 99.99999% of its repositories in Azure as agent-driven traffic and data center capacity constraints accelerate its infrastructure migration. This engineering breakdown explains how moving write coordination from entire repositories to individual references reduces contention, delivering 3–4x higher throughput in internal tests.

articles.headline: Introducing Claude Duet
articles.blurb: Anthropic has announced a research preview of Claude Duet, a new proactive agent app designed for professionals and small business owners. Built around Claude Opus 5.5, the app operates independently in the background via a virtual machine with its own browser to manage tasks, send daily briefs, and monitor connected apps. The application includes robust security frameworks and safety classifiers to safeguard sensitive user information before performing actions on their behalf.

articles.headline: ServiceNow and Nvidia launch Arc, a new AI agent for enterprise
articles.blurb: ServiceNow and Nvidia have launched Arc, a personal long-running AI agent built for enterprise use. Designed to run locally on Nvidia RTX Spark devices or within Nvidia OpenShell, Arc assists with daily tasks using productivity tools like email and Microsoft Teams. The companies emphasize a multi-level security framework that utilizes ServiceNow's Super Intelligence Control Tower, Nvidia OpenShell, and AI Passport to enforce runtime and hardware-layer policies and manage agent permissions.

articles.headline: Microsoft Entra ID ending native SMS authentication, pushing users to passkeys
articles.blurb: Microsoft has announced that it will retire its native SMS and voice authentication for Entra ID on February 1, 2027, for most customers, with the deadline extended to July 1, 2027, for Global Administrators and external users. Starting October 30, 2026, organizations will be able to choose a third-party telephony provider through the Microsoft Security Store. Microsoft recommends that organizations transition to phishing-resistant passkeys instead of relying on telephony-based authentication.

articles.headline: Crusoe heads to Paraguay for hydropowered AI compute
articles.blurb: Crusoe and Araico plan to build AI cloud infrastructure powered by Paraguay's Itaipú hydroelectric dam, with an initial deployment targeted for mid-2027. The project has a path to 106 MW of IT capacity and will serve both US customers and demand across Latin America.

articles.headline: Amazon Threat Intelligence identifies PHP2Shell exploitation prior to public disclosure in MadPot
articles.blurb: The company advises security teams to measure mitigation timelines in hours, investigate from the earliest known exploitation date, and invest in signature-independent detections.

articles.headline: GitHub begins enforcing global Copilot feature defaults
articles.blurb: Through October 26, GitHub is rolling out enforcement that sets eligible, unconfigured Copilot features according to an organization's global default policy while preserving explicit administrator choices.

articles.headline: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
articles.blurb: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

articles.headline: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
articles.blurb: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

articles.headline: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
articles.blurb: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

articles.headline: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
articles.blurb: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today's epic patch batch dwarfs September's record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.

articles.headline: FBI Arrests Executive at Ransomware Negotiation Firm
articles.blurb: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity.

articles.headline: ShinyHunters Extorted Boeing Spin-off Prior to Arrests
articles.blurb: A teenager from Amman, Jordan suspected of leading the prolific data theft and extortion group ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the hacking gang. KrebsOnSecurity has learned that the suspect, who uses the hacker handle "Rey," was detained as ShinyHunters was in the process of extorting a business unit recently divested by the global aerospace company Boeing, which manufactures the fleet of planes used by the employer of Rey's father -- Royal Jordanian Airlines.

articles.headline: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
articles.blurb: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters. In the days immediately following the suspect's arrest, remaining ShinyHunters members dramatically escalated their attacks, stealing highly sensitive data from the FBI and extorting the Russian ransomware group Cl0p.

articles.headline: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
articles.blurb: A U.S. Army soldier who pleaded guilty to hacking into multiple telecommunications companies and stealing mobile call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers in 2024 was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison today and ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution to victims.

articles.headline: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight
articles.blurb: The consumer data broker Radaris.com has long had a reputation for ignoring requests to remove personal information from its vast empire of people-search services online. That reputation caught up with the company recently in a lawsuit alleging Radaris violated a New Jersey privacy law that provides for hefty fines against data brokers that publish personal information on state law enforcement officials. In the face of repeated stonewalling and prevarication by attorneys for Radaris, the judge in the case ordered that radaris.com and more than a dozen other data broker domains be transferred to the plaintiffs.

articles.headline: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
articles.blurb: Microsoft Corp. today issued updates to plug at least 974 security holes in its Windows operating systems and other software, by far its biggest single patch batch ever. Microsoft says artificial intelligence is helping to speed the discovery of vulnerabilities, but security experts warn that many organizations already are struggling to prioritize the more human-intensive endeavor of testing and deploying so many fixes each month.
